The Science · What do we know?

Follow the evidence.

A practical guide to separating human clinical evidence, preclinical promise, mechanism, community attention and regulatory status—without collapsing them into one score.

Our rule: a mechanism is not an outcome. An animal study is not a human trial. Popularity is not proof.
Explore the evidence

Four lanes. Four different questions.

The most useful way to read biohacking science is to know which kind of evidence you are actually looking at.

What has actually been tested in people?

Randomized trials, controlled studies, meaningful endpoints and indication-specific evidence.

Open Evidence Ledger →

What looks promising before human validation?

Animal models and laboratory work can reveal biology without proving benefit in people.

Human vs. preclinical →

Why might it work?

Mechanistic plausibility helps explain a hypothesis. It does not establish a clinical outcome.

How we rate evidence →

What are people talking about?

Attention and recurring anecdotes are tracked separately from efficacy and safety evidence.
